clue.text: Defendant's pleading to recover contents of 11?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in old English law, a defendant's answer to the plaintiff's surrejoinder
second meaning, read as RE- plus a verb: to spread the slices from the toast rack with butter once more

explanation.surface: A legal query about what a defendant pleads in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning second half: 11 is TOAST RACK, so its contents are toast, and to 're-butter' them is to coat them again.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebutter is the formal reply a defendant files in old common-law pleading, following the surrejoinder.

clue.text: For relaxing treatment, depend on priest — not acute

parts.note: to rest on something is to depend on it
a curé is a French parish priest; dropping the acute accent leaves the plain letters

explanation.surface: Advice to rely on a clergyman for a soothing therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not acute' sounds medical, matching the treatment, but it only removes the accent from the French priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest cure is a medical regime of enforced rest and quiet, prescribed as a treatment for nervous exhaustion.

clue.text: National emblem keen-eyed type uncovered first

indicators.note: first says the word just before it goes at the front, ahead of the bird

parts.note: with no covering on top, as a hairless head is
the eagle is proverbially sharp-sighted, hence 'eagle-eyed'

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed national symbol is revealed before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird's white head only looks bare; that is how it got its name.
explanation.definitionFit: This white-headed bird of prey was adopted as the symbol of the United States and appears on its Great Seal.

clue.text: Not, to put it another way, very fast

indicators.note: putting a word another way means writing it in the opposite direction, here upward in a down light

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
the direction the word is written in this down entry: upward

explanation.surface: Someone rephrasing a refusal, with an aside about great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light, 'not' read upward is the answer's description of itself: the word is written up the grid. A ton is 100 mph in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A ton-up is British slang for travelling at a hundred miles an hour, the mark of a reckless motorcyclist.

clue.text: Start off men getting on coach?

definitions.text: Start off men getting on coach?

parts.words: Start off men getting on coach?
parts.note: surface reading: a sports coach beginning a session with his players

parts.words: Start off men getting on coach?
parts.note: setter's reading: a coach is a railway carriage, so the whole clue is sending troops off by train

explanation.surface: A trainer getting his squad going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a sports trainer, but it is a railway carriage; the question mark signals the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain troops is to put them aboard a train for departure, which is starting men off on a railway carriage.

clue.text: Nut-producer ready to join partnership

parts.note: ready money, or 'the readies', is cash
East and West form a partnership at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Someone investing cash in a nut-farming business.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players sit as two pairs, North-South and East-West, so a partnership can be NS or EW.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a tropical tree whose kidney-shaped seed is the familiar edible nut, so it produces nuts.

clue.text: Often ran wildly round ring — fatal for Hemingway

indicators.note: wildly says the words before it are thrown into disorder
round says those mixed letters wrap around the next item

parts.note: these eight letters rearranged
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A frequent wild runner and a ring, somehow lethal to Ernest Hemingway.
explanation.walkthrough: Hemingway wrote Death in the Afternoon, his book on bullfighting, so the afternoon is the time that was fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's bullfighting book is titled Death in the Afternoon, so this time of day is the fatal one in his title.

clue.text: Found out, caught, and tried

definitions.meaning: second meaning: picked up a sound
third meaning: a case listened to by a judge in court

explanation.surface: A criminal discovered, arrested and put on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words read as a police sequence, but each is a separate sense of one past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of a listening verb covers learning news, catching a sound, and a judge hearing a court case.

clue.text: Operative's dropped right in the middle of Surrey

indicators.note: dropped says a letter falls out of the word, and the clue names which

parts.note: operative means in working order
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A worker has lost their way in central Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London; its town Woking sits near the middle of it, so the definition is a place, not a position.
explanation.definitionFit: Woking is a commuter town lying in the heart of the county, so it is found in central Surrey.

clue.text: Irritated person has this support

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an angry person is said to have their ..., like a bristling cat
second meaning: reinforcement held in reserve

explanation.surface: An annoyed person has backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone irritated has their hackles raised, idiomatically their back up, while reserve help or reinforcement is also called backup.

clue.text: In Paris, a long-established artistic event

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, across their joins

parts.note: the letters running across the end of the city, the article and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A venerable cultural fixture in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' looks like scene-setting, and fittingly the Paris Salon was the great official French art show, but 'In' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is an exhibition of living artists' work, after the official annual Paris Salon of the French Academy.

clue.text: Browning prepared what it contains, piece by piece

definitions.text: Browning prepared what it contains, piece by piece

parts.note: surface reading: the poet Robert Browning composing verses one at a time

parts.words: Browning prepared what it contains, piece by piece
parts.note: setter's reading: browning is grilling bread, and the holder keeps the slices apart one by one

explanation.surface: The poet Browning writing a collection piece by piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised at the start, 'Browning' looks like the poet, but it is what a grill does to bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast rack is a slotted holder that stands browned bread slices upright and separate at the breakfast table.

clue.text: Inferior by contrast with the dear queen?

parts.words: by contrast with the dear queen?
parts.note: surface reading: comparing someone with a beloved monarch

parts.words: by contrast with the dear queen?
parts.note: setter's reading: the opposite of dear is cheap and the card below the queen is the jack

explanation.surface: Something second-rate set beside a beloved queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' means expensive, not beloved, and the queen is a playing card, so each word is swapped for its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapjack describes shoddy, low-quality goods, originally those sold by a hawker of cheap wares.

clue.text: French master at home on the staff

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another is placed after it, so the second item comes first

parts.note: a staff is a rod
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A French schoolmaster living on the school staff.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts A after B.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was the great French sculptor of The Thinker, a master of his art.

clue.text: Reign after internal reform, with me in administration

indicators.note: an internal reform reshapes only the inside, so the middle letters are rearranged while the ends stay put
in places the following word inside the rearranged one

parts.note: the first and last letters stay, the inner three are rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch's rule, internally reformed, now includes the speaker in government.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is an older word for a system of government or rule, as well as a prescribed course of treatment.

clue.text: Legal notes made in error about Moriarty's assistant

indicators.note: something in error is wrongly arranged, so these letters must be put in a new order
about means the shuffled letters go around the next item

parts.note: these four letters rearranged and split around the next piece
Colonel Sebastian Moran is Professor Moriarty's henchman in the Sherlock Holmes stories

explanation.surface: Legal papers drawn up wrongly about a criminal's sidekick.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Moran, the crack shot in The Empty House, was chief of staff to Moriarty.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda are written records or notes, and in law a memorandum is a document recording the terms of an agreement.

clue.text: It helps actor to have fun in small part

indicators.note: in puts one word inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: PT is the short form of part
a romp is boisterous fun

explanation.surface: An actor enjoying themselves in a minor role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small part' suggests a bit role on stage, but it is just the abbreviation of part.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt is the whispered line or cue that helps a forgetful actor on stage remember the words.

clue.text: Grant, for example, minimal amount to tenant

parts.note: a penny, abbreviated P, is the smallest sum
a tenant is a resident of a property

explanation.surface: A small grant of money given to a tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a sum handed over, but it is Ulysses S. Grant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S. Grant, the Union general, became the eighteenth head of state of the United States.

clue.text: Rum sounding type, possibly, my words offend

parts.note: my words are said by me, the speaker I
slander is spoken words that offend by defaming

explanation.surface: An odd-sounding character confesses their words cause offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like an adjective meaning odd, but Rum is a small island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, with sounds (sea channels) around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or inhabitant of the Hebridean island of Rum is one example of someone living on an island.

clue.text: Widow's donation, mostly  for singularly pious type

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a widow is a woman, so her possessive
the widow's mite is the tiny gift praised by Jesus in the Gospels

explanation.surface: A widow's small gift goes mostly to a religious recluse.
explanation.walkthrough: The widow's mite is the poor widow's two small coins in Mark 12, praised above rich men's gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit is a religious recluse who lives alone for devotion, so a single pious person.

clue.text: Champion boxer, perhaps

parts.note: surface reading: a title-holding prizefighter
setter's reading: a boxer is a breed of hound, and the best of them is the winner

explanation.surface: A boxing title-holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' is a dog breed, and 'perhaps' warns it is only one example of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Top dog is an idiom for the winner or most powerful person, literally the leading canine.

clue.text: Handles four-in-hand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: touches or toys with
second meaning: a hand has four of these digits besides the thumb

explanation.walkthrough: A four-in-hand is a coach drawn by four horses, matching 'handles' as driving; here it is read literally as four digits on a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means touching with the hand, and a hand holds four of these digits beside its thumb.

clue.text: Supervisors? Just characters in novel, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the letters are what the phrase sounds like spoken

parts.note: Edgar Wallace's thriller The Four Just Men features a quartet of vigilantes

explanation.surface: Bosses who are merely fictional characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' seems to mean merely, but it belongs to the title The Four Just Men.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremen are workers placed in charge of a gang or shop floor, so they act as supervisors.

clue.text: Crown Court action about short measure

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other

parts.note: a lawsuit is an action in court
mm is the short form of millimetre

explanation.surface: A Crown Court case about a shopkeeper giving short measure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crown Court is the English criminal court, so 'Crown' seems glued to 'Court', but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of a hill is its top, the highest point or peak.

clue.text: Superior part of Oxford

definitions.meaning: first meaning: higher in rank or position
second meaning: an oxford is a laced shoe, and this is the part above the sole

explanation.surface: Someone or something rated higher in the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the city, but an oxford is a lace-up leather shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means higher in rank, and also names the part of a shoe above the sole.

clue.text: Tangled ropes could be this

indicators.note: tangled things are twisted out of order, so the next word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A knotted mess of rope is hard to undo.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a snarl of rope is a puzzle to unpick.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a baffling problem, which is just what a tangle of rope presents to anyone trying to undo it.

clue.text: A head's translation

parts.note: surface reading: a headmaster's rendering of a text
setter's reading: the phrase 'a head', meaning each, put into Latin

explanation.surface: A headteacher's version of some foreign text.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as possession by a head teacher, but it means 'a head is the translation of' the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase per capita literally means by heads, used for each person, as in income per head.

clue.text: In case of serious complaint, right to claim

indicators.note: in the case of means placed inside the next word as its casing

parts.note: ague is a malarial fever
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone with a serious illness has the right to make a claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case of' sounds like insurance wording, but it puts the letter inside the fever.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue a point is to maintain or assert it, so it means to claim.

clue.text: Deceive maiden before I fall for another one

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written
the Fall in Eden was the first sin
taken as written
another maiden, so M again

explanation.surface: A maiden warned not to be fooled by a second suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall for' reads as a phrase meaning be taken in, but the two words work separately, and 'another one' repeats the maiden's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To misinform someone is to give them false information, so it means to mislead or deceive them.

clue.text: Desire for something — with a start, it's done!

indicators.note: with a start says the phrase that follows is the answer with a letter added at the front, so remove it

parts.note: the cry when a bargain is struck

explanation.surface: Someone startled as their longed-for deal is completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a start' sounds like being startled, but it means put A at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is an excessive, selfish craving for something such as money or food, so a desire for it.

clue.text: Clue is removed from this study

indicators.note: removed from says the word before is taken out of the word after

parts.note: taken as written, with the two-letter word taken out
taken as written
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A crossword clue has been dropped from a piece of research.
explanation.definitionFit: A thread is a guiding line through a mystery, as in Ariadne's thread, so a hint or clue to follow.

clue.text: List contracts for this manufacturer

indicators.note: something that contracts gets shorter, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an inventory is a list of goods

explanation.surface: A list of contracts drawn up for a factory owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' looks like a noun for legal agreements, but it is the verb shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventor is one who devises or makes up new things, an older sense of manufacture being to fabricate.
